# Copantry

> Copantry is a meal planner, pantry tracker and shopping-list app for
> households that decides what's for dinner from the food you already have and
> builds your shopping list automatically — so you cook more, waste less and
> never scramble at 6pm. Web today; native Android and iOS apps coming soon. UI
> in English, French, Italian, Portuguese, German and Spanish; recipes stay in
> their original language.

- Website: https://www.copantry.com
- App: https://app.copantry.com
- API: https://api.copantry.com
- MCP endpoint: https://api.copantry.com/mcp

## Core pages

- [What Copantry is](https://www.copantry.com/): decides what's for dinner from what you already have, then builds the shopping list — one shared app for the whole household. Cooking more and wasting less is the built-in bonus.
- [How it works](https://www.copantry.com/how-it-works): knows what you have → tells you what to cook → buys only what's missing.
- [Reduce food waste](https://www.copantry.com/features/reduce-food-waste): expiry tracking and use-it-up meal suggestions.
- [Meal planning](https://www.copantry.com/features/meal-planning): plan a week around your pantry, not an empty calendar.
- [Pantry tracking](https://www.copantry.com/features/pantry-tracking): live inventory added by photo, receipt, voice or text.
- [Shopping lists](https://www.copantry.com/features/shopping-lists): auto-built from your plan minus your pantry, aisle-sorted.
- [How Copantry is different](https://www.copantry.com/why-copantry): vs calendar-first planners, recipe-savers and basic list apps.

## For AI assistants & agents

- [Plan from ChatGPT or Claude (MCP)](https://www.copantry.com/features/ai-assistant-mcp): drive Copantry from an MCP-compatible assistant.
- [Full MCP tool reference](https://www.copantry.com/llms-full.txt): every MCP tool, its parameters and when to use it.

## Learn

- [How long does food last?](https://www.copantry.com/learn): shelf-life, storage and use-it-up guides per ingredient.
- [Blog](https://www.copantry.com/blog): cooking what you have, the use-it-up method, household food-waste data.
